sentences.text: Asilisaurus kongwe is the type species of an extinct genus of silesaurid archosaurs.
Specimens of this lightly built animal measured between one and three meters in length and stood between half a meter and one meter tall.

The skull featured a unique lack of teeth at the front of the premaxilla and a downturned, toothless tip on the lower jaw, while the premaxilla possessed only a single tooth at the rear near the maxilla.
Its skeleton included two sacral vertebrae with individual sacral ribs, and the scapula was long, narrow, and expanded into a triangular tip without perforations.
The hip structure possessed a closed acetabulum, distinguishing it from the open acetabulum found in dinosaurs.
Asilisaurus was the first non-dinosaur dinosauromorph recovered from Africa and the first non-dinosaur dinosauriform discovered on the continent.
It holds the distinction of being the oldest known archosaur on the avian lineage discovered to date.
One femur specimen was estimated to be 29.6-39.6 cm long, more than twice the length of other known Asilisaurus femurs.
The first remains were found in 2007 at a bonebed near Litumba Ndyosi in Tanzania.

The genus was formally described in 2010 by a team of researchers from the United States, Germany, and South Africa, with the generic name derived from the Swahili word for 'ancestor' and the Greek word for 'lizard'.
The specific name kongwe means 'ancient' in Swahili.
Based on limb length, the animal probably walked on all four legs, apparently moving by walking on four legs.

Evidence of a beak and peg-like teeth suggests Asilisaurus was likely an omnivore or herbivore, with the conical shape of its teeth suggesting that fish may have been part of its diet, while research indicates it was unlikely to be a specialized carnivore or an obligate herbivore.

At least 14 individuals of Asilisaurus were present at the discovery site, including the holotype, with at least 14 specimens found in southern Tanzania dating to the Anisian stage of the Middle Triassic.

Studies of femurs revealed multiple polymorphic trajectories in muscle scar development rather than a universal sequence, and histological analysis showed no lines of arrested growth, even in large specimens, though researchers hypothesize that the absence of these lines does not mean specimens died within a year, as their growth rate was too slow for that.
Asilisaurus is classified within the family Silesauridae, which is its parent group.
It is also classified within the class Ornithischia.
Specimens were found in southern Tanzania dating to the Anisian stage of the Middle Triassic.
Some authors suggest the Manda Beds formation may date to the Ladinian or early Carnian stages instead of the Anisian.
Asilisaurus represents the first example of the avian lineage radiation during the Anisian period.
Researchers suggest that Asilisaurus implies dinosaurs may be older than previously thought.
